blocking.where: TRD.md Validation Commands (same order in TASKS.md Final Validation Commands and AGENTS.md Validation Gates)
blocking.why: The final gate order runs npm test before npm run build. The page-level tests (homepostlist, authorpage, postpage, packaging) read dist/ and fail when it is missing, as TRD CON-RUNTIME-WIRING says. A fresh checkout following the final gates in order therefore fails at step 2. Per-task validation lists the build first, so the documents contradict each other on the order. The same applies to a stale dist/.
blocking.fix: Reorder the final gates to check, build, test, test:a11y, audit:performance, in TRD, TASKS and AGENTS. Alternatively state that npm test must follow npm run build.

polish.quote: Every post page and author page is reachable by a link from the home page.
polish.why: The home page links authors only through post entries. An author with no posts has a page but no link from the home page, and no task or test covers this case.
polish.fix: Either restrict the sentence to authors that have posts, or add an authors list to the home page component and name its owner.

polish.quote: sorts the posts by data.published descending
polish.why: The tie-break for posts with the same publication date is unspecified. The home page and author pages could order them differently, and a test cannot assert a stable order.
polish.fix: Add a tie-break to the contract, such as the entry id descending, for both the home and author lists.

polish.why: The kit schema uses z.coerce.date(), which gives a UTC Date, and the post page formats it with toISOString(). The 'local calendar day' wording does not match this and invites timezone drift.
polish.fix: State that published is a YYYY-MM-DD string or UTC date rendered with toISOString().slice(0,10) everywhere.

polish.quote: a list field as one ol with one li per item in stored order
polish.why: Neither collection has a list field, so this is generic boilerplate that does not apply.
polish.fix: Remove the list-field clause from the TASK-05 prompt.

polish.quote: render them as one ul with one li per post
polish.why: The behavior for an author with zero posts is unspecified. It could be an empty ul, which is bad accessibility, or an omitted list, and a test cannot assert either.
polish.fix: Specify that an author with no posts renders no ul and shows no empty-state text, or add an empty-state line.

polish.why: The idea never mentions these, so the compiler added scope-exclusion text that pads the Problem Statement and Success framing without any task consequence.
polish.fix: Drop the invented non-goals, or reduce them to the single constraint that the site has no forms.

review.verdict: Nearly buildable. One blocking defect: the final validation order runs npm test before npm run build, so the dist-dependent tests fail on a clean tree. Fix that and the packet is coherent. Features, ownership, file creation and modification order, the data interface and the kit all agree, and the remaining items are polish.
